title: Devin post-compaction.cjs duplicates boundary bridge logic with hardcoded path — drift risk
scopeProof: grep -rn 'notifyDirectiveLifecycleBoundary|notifyLifecycleBoundary' .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp-server/hooks/ shows 7 adapters import the shared module; only devin/post-compaction.cjs implements a separate hardcoded-path function
description: The Devin PostCompaction adapter embeds its own notifyLifecycleBoundary() function that hardcodes the path to the compiled dist instead of importing the shared bridge module. This creates a drift risk: if the dist path changes, only Devin's adapter will break while the other 7 adapters continue working via upward-walk resolution.
recommendation: Replace the embedded notifyLifecycleBoundary in devin/post-compaction.cjs with an import from the shared bridge module, or at minimum use the same upward-walk resolution pattern from directive-lifecycle-boundary.ts:26-38.

claimAdjudication.claim: Devin post-compaction.cjs duplicates boundary bridge logic with hardcoded path, creating a drift risk separate from the 7 other adapters that use the shared import
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether Devin has a legitimate reason for a separate implementation (e.g., CJS vs ESM compatibility). The adapter is CJS while the shared bridge is ESM — but the adapter already uses execFileSync to spawn Node, and the shared bridge itself can be spawned identically. No architectural reason to duplicate.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The adapter predates the shared bridge module and was never updated to import it.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: If the embedded path is proven to be a documented intentional isolation boundary (not just legacy duplication), downgrade to P2.

title: No test coverage for the boundary bridge spawn itself
scopeProof: Full test file read (459 lines); search for 'boundary' in test file confirms only advanceDirectiveLifecycleBoundary is imported/tested, not notifyDirectiveLifecycleBoundary or the compiled dist
description: The test suite exercises advanceDirectiveLifecycleBoundary() directly with both InMemory and File stores, and tests cross-process epoch advancement via FileDirectiveLifecycleStore.advanceGeneration(). However, no test spawns the compiled dist as a child process or exercises notifyDirectiveLifecycleBoundary() end-to-end. The bridge's spawnSync call, upward-walk resolution, timeout, and SIGKILL behavior are untested.

title: Store hardening delegated entirely to Python helper — no pure-JS fallback
scopeProof: directive-lifecycle-file-store.ts:30-37 resolves helper or returns null; directive-lifecycle-file-store.ts:118 gates all operations on helper availability; no JS fallback path exists in the file
description: The FileDirectiveLifecycleStore delegates ALL operations to a Python script via spawnSync. If python3 is unavailable or the Python script is missing, the store fails open silently (all operations return null → full directive delivery). While fail-open is correct, there is no documented pure-JS fallback or explicit runtime requirement that python3 must be available for durable suppression to work.

description: No automated build verification step — if a developer edits the TS source but forgets to rebuild, the stale dist would silently fail.
Devin post-compaction.cjs hardcodes a path that differs from the shared bridge's upward-walk resolution.
The durable store requires python3 at runtime. Without it, the store fails open silently.
The notifyDirectiveLifecycleBoundary() return value is not checked by ANY caller (fail-open by design).
